{{< include _elements-kit.qmd >}}

**Articulation** is *how* a note is played: how it starts, how long it lasts and how it joins the next one. It is not how
loud it is (that is [dynamics](elements-dynamics.qmd)). The same eight notes can sound bouncy, smooth or
aggressive depending on articulation alone.

## 1. Staccato and legato

**Staccato** means short and detached. You hear a gap after each note. It is written as a dot above or below the notehead
(on the opposite side from the stem).

**Legato** means smooth, with no breaks between the notes. A **slur** (a curved line over or under notes of *different*
pitches) asks for legato.

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Staccato
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
.C .E .G .c|.G .E .C z|]
</script><script type="text/plain" data-bend>
{"bpm":100,"sound":"piano","notes":[{"t":0,"d":0.35,"midi":60},{"t":1,"d":0.35,"midi":64},{"t":2,"d":0.35,"midi":67},{"t":3,"d":0.35,"midi":72},{"t":4,"d":0.35,"midi":67},{"t":5,"d":0.35,"midi":64},{"t":6,"d":0.35,"midi":60}]}
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Legato (slurred)
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
(C E G c|G E C) z|]
</script><script type="text/plain" data-bend>
{"bpm":100,"sound":"piano","notes":[{"t":0,"d":1.08,"midi":60},{"t":1,"d":1.08,"midi":64},{"t":2,"d":1.08,"midi":67},{"t":3,"d":1.08,"midi":72},{"t":4,"d":1.08,"midi":67},{"t":5,"d":1.08,"midi":64},{"t":6,"d":1,"midi":60}]}
</script></div>
:::

<div class="el-recap">
<strong>Slur or tie?</strong> Both are curves. A curve joining two notes of the <em>same</em> pitch is a <strong>tie</strong>: play
one note, held for both lengths. A curve over <em>different</em> pitches is a <strong>slur</strong>: play them all, smoothly.
</div>

**How players make a slur**

| Instrument | Legato / slurred | Detached |
|---|---|---|
| Strings (violin, cello…) | all the slurred notes in one bow stroke, no change of direction | a new bow stroke (or a lifted bow) for each note |
| Woodwind and brass | tongue only the first note; the rest change by fingers (or slide) alone | tongue every note |
| Voice | one breath, the vowel kept going between notes | a little stop of the breath or a consonant on each note |
| Piano | hold each key until the next one is down | lift each finger early |

## 2. Accents and other marks

An **accent** (`>`) asks for extra force on the start of the note. Marks can be combined: a staccato dot *and* an accent
means short and strong.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Accents on the first beat of each measure, then staccato and accented together
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
!>!G B d B|!>!c A F A|!>!.G .B !>!.d z|]
</script></div>

| Sign | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.` over/under the notehead | staccato | short, detached |
| `>` | accent | strong start |
| `-` (a short line) | tenuto | hold for its full length, a slight weight |
| `^` | marcato | stronger than an accent |
| curve over different notes | slur | legato |
| straight or wavy line between two notes, often marked *gliss.* | glissando | slide from one to the other |

## 3. Glissando

A **glissando** is a slide from one note to another. On a violin, trombone or voice it is a smooth slide through every
pitch in between. On a piano or harp it is a sweep across the keys or strings.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="70"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:A violin slides up a fifth
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
!slide!D A|]
</script><script type="text/plain" data-bend>
{"bpm":70,"sound":"violin","notes":[{"t":0,"d":3.6,"midi":62,"bend":[[0,0],[1.2,0],[2,7]]}]}
</script></div>

## 4. Playing techniques

Some articulations change the *kind* of sound an instrument makes. Each is a word above the staff.

| Technique | Who | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Pizzicato** (*pizz.*) | strings | pluck the strings; *arco* goes back to the bow |
| **Double stopping** | strings | two strings at once |
| **Con sordino** (*con sord.*) | strings, brass | play with a mute; *senza sord.* takes it off |
| **Tremolo** | strings (and others) | repeat one note very fast (a trembling sound) |
| **Vibrato** | strings, voice, wind, brass | let the pitch waver a little, for warmth |
| **Falsetto** | voice | a light, high register above the normal voice, used mostly by men |

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-sound="violin" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Arco (bowed)
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:D
D F A d|A F D2|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-sound="pizzicato_strings" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Pizzicato (plucked)
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:D
D F A d|A F D2|]
</script></div>
:::

## 5. Writing your own

- Choose the articulation for what you want the listener to feel: staccato for light or playful, legato for calm or sad,
  accents to push the beat or make a rhythm stand out.
- Put articulation *on the notes*; [dynamics](elements-dynamics.qmd) go under the staff.
- Check each mark with a player of that instrument: a slur on a trumpet is easy, a slur across a big leap on a trombone is not.
